_what: The show's own frames, measured by tools/measure_frame.py, and the tolerances derived from them. This is the corpus behind measure_frame.DIST_BAND, CRUSHED_ENVELOPE and CLIPPED_CAP. Regenerate and re-check with `python3 tools/measure_frame.py --derive`; that command fails if the module's constants have stopped describing what is in here.
_why: Every exposure in this project was set by a MEDIAN test against a reference frame -- x1.40 +/-25%. The owner looked at the renders and said they read as blockout while every gate was green, and both were true: a median says where the middle of a picture sits and nothing about how far it reaches. docs/engine-drum-garden.png sits at x1.49 of garden.png (green) with p5 at 3.2x the reference's and 0.01% of the frame black against the reference's 5.63%.

method.corpus: 32 deduplicated authority-1 on-screen frames that depict a lit SET or a lit exterior -- the thing our renders are. Props on a studio backdrop, schematics, costume stills, fan reconstructions and both QUARANTINE folders are excluded. Byte-identical duplicates counted once.
method.pair_rule: Two show frames whose medians agree within TOL (+/-25%) are treated as the same lighting register measured twice. This is NOT a new judgement: it is the rule export_scene.DRUM_CALIBRATION already applies when it accepts garden.png against Babylon_5_2-22_34b.jpg (8% apart) and rejects 33a and 29a.
method.statistic: For each qualifying pair and each statistic, |ln(a/b)|. The band is the p95 of that distribution, so each band admits 95% of the disagreement the show has with itself at matched level.
method.why_not_max: The maximum of 121 samples is one pair, not a tolerance. Using it would fit an envelope to the single worst case and the gate could never fail.
method.why_not_p90: At p90 the combined verdict rejects 27% of the pairs the show itself produces. A gate that fails a quarter of the reference material is measuring the material.
method.application: A render is compared against its reference RE-EXPOSED TO RENDER_OFFSET -- measure(ref, gain=1.40) -- so the level offset the median gate already allows is not charged again as a shape difference. Scaling the IMAGE is not the same as scaling the STATISTICS: it lifts sub-floor pixels into the measurable set where they arrive at the bottom and hold p5 down. garden.png p5 goes 0.0180 -> 0.0178 under x1.40, not to 0.0252.
method.clipped: No usable pairwise structure -- two median-agreeing show frames disagree on clipped fraction by x53 at p90 and x134 at the maximum. Gated as an absolute cap at the p95 of the corpus's clipped fraction at the offset instead.
method.crushed_envelope: The ratio band alone is blind at both ends: x11.52 of nearly nothing is still nearly nothing, and against a reference that crushes half the frame it permits a render that is 90% black. The envelope is the min and max the corpus itself occupies at the offset.

It was MISSED on the first pass of this corpus and added when the tree was re-enumerated file by file. Adding one frame in 33 moved the p5 band from x1.224 to x1.290, which is the honest measure of how stable a 33-frame estimate is: p95 of a 124-pair sample is the 6th-largest value and one new frame contributes 26 new pairs.

clipped_note: Absolute, one-sided, and derived from the corpus's OWN clipped fraction at the offset rather than from a pairwise band: the pairwise dispersion of clipped over the 121 pairs is x2.78 at p50, x7.83 at p68 and x53.7 at p90, which is no structure at all. 3.69% independently corroborates the 4% overexposure threshold report() already carried, which was derived from our own lamp geometry clipping 1.3-3.1%.

show_vs_show_note:
THE GATE RUN ON THE SHOW AGAINST ITSELF, which is the only validation that means anything: for each of the 124 median-agreeing pairs, in both orders (248 trials), one frame stands in for our render and the other for its reference.
  * `at_gain_1.0` is where the four RATIO bands were derived, and there they admit 93.5-94.4% -- the ~95% they were built for. The `crushed in show range` and `clipped under cap` rows in that block are meaningless: both thresholds are measured at the offset and this block is not at it.
  * `at_the_offset` is the form the gate is APPLIED in -- the reference side is always measure(ref, gain=RENDER_OFFSET). There the envelope admits 100% and the cap 94.4% (both by construction, being derived from that population), p95 100%, p5/p95 96.8%, p5 91.1% and crushed 85.5%. The crushed band loses ten points because it was estimated at gain 1.0 and is applied to a GAINED reference, and gaining changes a censored fraction nonlinearly. That is a known and stated looseness in one of the six checks, not a hidden one.
  * THE COMBINED VERDICT ADMITS 77.4% (192 of 248). Six checks at 85-100% cannot combine to 95%. Loosening them until it did would require each at ~99%, which is the observed maximum, which is an envelope and not a tolerance. Part of the missing 23% is also real: the 124 pairs include a war room against a residential corridor, which agree on median by coincidence and are not the same picture at all.
median_exposure_response_note: d(ln median)/d(ln gain) between x1.0 and x1.4, measured by scaling each reference frame's LINEAR luminance. If measure_frame's median were proportional to exposure this would be 1.0 everywhere. It ranges 0.97 (Babylon_5_2-22_34b.jpg) to 0.01 (more zocalo.png), and 7 of 33 frames go DOWN somewhere in x0.5..x2.0 -- rotunda.webp -0.46, Starfury.jpg -0.37, sleeping-in-light-05.jpg -0.29, babylon 5 welcome sign...jpg -0.16, conference aerea.webp -0.11, more hallway.jpg +0.06 non-monotone, more zocalo.png +0.01 non-monotone. CAUSE: raising exposure recruits sub-floor pixels into the measurable set and they arrive at the BOTTOM. CONSEQUENCE: every value in export_scene.ROOM_EXPOSURE and BESPOKE_EXPOSURE was obtained from `gain *= 1.40 * ref_median / our_median`, which assumes this exponent is 1. On the customs reference it is negative. STATE.md already records the symptom for the plant -- 'it sits at 1.59x either way' -- and attributes it to that room; it is a property of the statistic.

reverification._what: Every exposure in tools/export_scene.py that has a committed frame and a recorded reference, re-measured with the distribution comparison. old_verdict is the median test the exposure was SET by; new_verdict is the whole-distribution test. NO EXPOSURE VALUE WAS CHANGED to produce this table -- the point of it is to say how far off we are.
reverification._headline: 17 of 17 pass the old median test. 1 of 17 passes the new whole-distribution test. The single pass is docs/engine-market.png against more zocalo.png, and it is the evidence that the gate is not simply rejecting everything. p5 fails on 13 of 17; the crushed ratio on 4; the crushed envelope on 3; p95 on 2; p5/p95 on 3; the clipped cap on none.

_not_verifiable.ROOM_EXPOSURE: 9 of the 11 archetype exposures have NO COMMITTED FRAME and therefore cannot be re-verified at all: industrial, store, transit, hospitality, worship, research, detention, office, generic. Only medical (docs/engine-medlab.png) and commerce (docs/engine-market.png) were committed. Their values were set from renders that were measured and then discarded.
_not_verifiable.EXTERIOR_CALIBRATION night: No reference frame exists -- export_scene says so explicitly and refuses to record a `reference` key. The distribution comparison cannot be run. What can be said: docs/engine-exterior-night.png is 97.92% crushed, against 37.22% for `Cobra Bays with starfurries.webp` and 42.08% for `Starfury.jpg` at the same offset -- outside the corpus envelope, but the frame is 9.2 km of mostly empty starfield and the statistic is content-dominated at that framing.
_not_verifiable.exterior day reference: `exterior more.jpg` is authority 2, a render of the production CGI model, and is NOT a member of the corpus the bands were derived from -- the corpus is broadcast frames only. Its distribution verdict is reported for information; the bands were not derived from production renders and may not describe one.
